subject: Post-demo: Retrieval configs, reranker shortlist, and QA benchmarks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@brightpathhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Retrieval configs, reranker shortlist, and QA benchmarks

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the walkthrough of your user flows. Per our demo, I wanted to capture the concrete next steps we discussed and propose an initial RAG test plan so we can validate model fit & grounding risk early. High-level recap: 

- Goal: accurate, auditable answers to clinician questions from BrightPath's internal guidelines (low hallucination tolerance).
- Primary KPI: grounding precision (@turn) and factual fidelity measured against a 500-item prompt set we will co-curate.
- Latency target: 300ms median generator latency for single-turn clinician queries.

Proposed next steps (attached spreadsheet has the test matrix):
1) We’ll run 3 model families for the generator: redwood-v4-small, redwood-v4-medium-quant, and an Llama-compat baseline (for cost comparison).
2) Retrieval configs to compare in first sweep: exact-match sparse (BM25) vs. embedding ANN (FAISS) with 3 window sizes (top_k: 5/15/50).
3) Reranker shortlist: our internal lightweight cross-encoder, and a heavier pairwise BERT ranker. The spreadsheet marks expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
4) Quality controls: prompt templates, negative prompts, and a small eval harness to flag regression vs. your golden answers.

Please confirm the sample prompt set we should seed (I attached an initial 80 prompts based on the flows you showed). If that looks good, we’ll schedule the sweep for next week and share a short dashboard with grounding metrics (precision@k, hallucination rate, and a qualitative sample set).

Attaching: bp-rag-testplan-v1.xlsx, bp_sample_prompts_v2.txt

Thanks —
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Retrieval configs, reranker shortlist, and QA benchmarks

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and aligns with what we talked about. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 500-item gold set sounds right but can we start with 200 high-frequency clinician Qs for the first sweep? We want quick signal.
- For retrieval, our infra team prefers embedding-based retrieval into FAISS; can you include a run with chunking at 1-paragraph vs. 3-paragraphs?
- On rerankers — cost matters; Samir & I would like to see the lightweight cross-encoder first and only escalate to the BERT pairwise if precision is lacking.

We reviewed the sample prompts and made inline notes in bp_sample_prompts_v2.txt (minor edits).

Samir and I are available Friday morning if you want to sync for 30m before you kick off the runs.

Best,
Alice Turner
Director, Clinical Platforms
BrightPath Health

Hey Alice — happy to join Friday. Quick additional notes from the product side so expectations are clear: 

- Measurement: our dashboard will surface grounding precision@5, hallucination rate (binary human label), average token cost, and median backend latency by model/config. We’ll also include a small “surprise” prompt subset to test brittleness. 
- Rollout: if results look good on the 200-sample sweep, we typically recommend a canary with 5% traffic for a week before broad rollout.
- Compliance: BrightPath mentioned audit logs — we’ll provide request/response IDs and a snapshot of retrieval traces for any flagged failures.

I’ve flagged the spreadsheet with the canary plan and updated the expected run times for the BERT pairwise reranker. See the Drive link in the metadata.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: Retrieval configs, reranker shortlist, and QA benchmarks

Looping back after a quick infra check — a couple of engineering constraints and suggested defaults to make the sweep lowest-effort: 

- Indexing: recommend paragraph-level chunking (approximately 150-300 tokens) as default; we’ll run the 3-paragraph variant as requested by Alice but it will increase index size ~2.7x.
- ANN settings: use FAISS HNSW, efSearch=64 for initial runs to balance recall/latency.
- Reranker: run the lightweight cross-encoder at top_k=50 then evaluate precision@5 before queueing the expensive pairwise BERT.
- Seed prompts: I’ll normalize the prompt templates to ensure deterministic pass/fail for the regression harness.

I’ll kick off the sweep Friday afternoon (PST) and share the initial results dashboard Monday. If we want a 30m sync Friday 9:30am PST to align, I can join.

- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
